objective.statement: Group notes so that every beat of compound time can be seen.
successCriteria: I beam three quavers together in each beat.
I write a whole beat as one dotted crotchet and two beats as one dotted minim.
I tie a note that crosses a beat, so the beat stays clear.

explanation.text: Good grouping lets a player see each beat at a glance. In compound time, each beat is a dotted crotchet, so every beat should be easy to spot.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 6/8: six quavers in two beamed groups of three; then a dotted crotchet and a group of three quavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver), 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver). Bar 2: dotted crotchet, 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver).

explanation.caption: Beam the quavers of each beat together. Do not join groups from different beats.

explanation.text: A note can be written as a single note only if it sits inside one beat, or fills whole beats from one beat line to another. A crotchet and a quaver in one beat are written separately, a crotchet then a quaver.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 6/8: a dotted minim; then a dotted crotchet, a crotchet and a quaver.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted minim. Bar 2: dotted crotchet, crotchet, quaver.

explanation.caption: Two whole beats are one dotted minim, not two dotted crotchets joined by a tie.

explanation.text: When a long sound begins or ends in the middle of a beat, split it into two notes and join them with a tie. The tie shows where the beat line falls. Do not use a tie where a single note would do. Show every beat: beam in threes, use a dotted minim for two whole beats, and tie only where a note would hide the beat.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 6/8: a dotted crotchet tied to a quaver, then a crotchet. The tie crosses the beat line.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted crotchet tied to, quaver, crotchet.

explanation.caption: A dotted crotchet tied to a quaver: the tie crosses into the second beat.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 9/8: a beat of three beamed quavers, a dotted crotchet, then another beat of three beamed quavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver), dotted crotchet, 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver).

steps: Count the three beats: three quavers, one dotted crotchet, three quavers.
Each group of three quavers has its own beam.
No beam crosses from one beat to the next, so all three beats are visible.

music.textAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet, quaver, quaver, quaver, quaver, dotted crotchet, crotchet, quaver. Bar 2: crotchet, quaver, quaver, quaver, quaver, dotted crotchet, crotchet, quaver. Bar 3: crotchet, quaver, quaver, quaver, quaver, crotchet tied to, quaver, crotchet, quaver.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet, quaver, 2 beamed together (quaver, quaver), quaver, dotted crotchet, crotchet, quaver. Bar 2: crotchet, quaver, 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver), dotted crotchet, crotchet, quaver. Bar 3: crotchet, quaver, 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver), crotchet tied to, quaver, crotchet, quaver.

1.reason: The three quavers of a beat belong together. Beam all three, not two and one.

3.reason: A tie inside one beat is not needed: a dotted crotchet already shows the whole beat.

hints: Each beat is a dotted crotchet. Can you see every beat?
12/8 has four dotted-crotchet beats in each bar. Each beat should be easy to see.

feedback.correct: Yes: every beat can be seen.

mistakes.beam-across-middle: In four-beat bars, keep the two halves of the bar visible — don't beam across the middle.
mistakes.rest-across-beat: That rest hides where a beat begins. Use one rest to finish the beat, and another for the next.
mistakes.half-bar-rest-misplaced: A two-beat rest can fill the first or second half of a four-beat bar, but not the middle two beats.
mistakes.tie-instead-of-dot: A dotted note says the same thing more simply here.
mistakes.compound-beat-hidden: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Mark where each beat starts, then regroup.
